_why: SECOND held-out batch. Never used to choose or tune a change.
The first held-out batch (scenarios-heldout.json) was run once as a
baseline and scored 0.750 against the main set's 0.975. Its failures were
then read to diagnose general causes, and two consistency rules were
designed partly from that reading - which makes that batch tuned, in the
same way the main 40 are. A batch you have looked at while fixing things
So this batch was written after those two rules existed and BEFORE any run
of it, and before the first batch was re-run. It is the clean measurement
for the M14 changes. Same synthetic policy, same conventions as
scenarios.json, same author as the fixes (so not fully independent), and
situations that appear in neither the main set nor the first batch.

cases.scenario: I fractured my ankle while mountaineering in the Himalayas and needed surgery. I have held the policy seven years.
cases.why: Treatment necessitated by hazardous or adventure sports is excluded, and mountaineering is named.

cases.scenario: I want the policy to pay for a contraceptive implant. I have held it three years.
cases.why: Any form of contraception is excluded.

cases.scenario: I had cataract surgery a year after buying the policy.
cases.why: Cataract is a specified disease with a twenty four month waiting period; a year is short of it.

cases.scenario: I gave birth four years after taking out the policy. It was my first delivery.
cases.why: Maternity is covered after thirty six months of continuous cover, limited to two deliveries in a lifetime. Four years clears the wait and this is the first delivery.

cases.scenario: I crashed my scooter while drunk and broke my wrist. I have held the policy six years.
cases.why: Expenses attributable to the use of alcohol are excluded.

cases.scenario: My sum insured is 3 lakh and I was in intensive care for two days at 9,000 rupees a day. I have held the policy six years.
cases.why: ICU charges are capped at 2% of the sum insured per day, which is 6,000; 9,000 exceeds it, so the excess is not paid.

cases.scenario: I bought the policy when I was 57, six years ago, and was admitted for pneumonia last week.
cases.why: The co-payment applies only to someone who had completed sixty at inception; 57 had not. Six years clears every waiting period and pneumonia is not excluded.

cases.scenario: I was admitted in an emergency and my family informed the insurer within twelve hours. I have held the policy five years.
cases.why: Emergency admissions need notice within twenty four hours; twelve hours meets it. Nothing described is excluded or capped.

cases.scenario: I had physiotherapy sixty days after being discharged, for the same condition, and my in-patient claim was accepted. I have held the policy four years.
cases.why: Post-hospitalisation expenses are covered for ninety days after discharge, for the same condition, where the in-patient claim was accepted. Sixty days is inside the window.

cases.scenario: I need deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease. My sum insured is 10 lakh and I have held the policy eight years.
cases.why: Deep brain stimulation is named in the modern treatment limit, restricted to 50% of the sum insured per policy year.

cases.scenario: Does this policy cover vet bills for my dog?
cases.why: A health policy for people does not address animals at all. The document is silent, not negative.

cases.scenario: After losing a lot of weight I had surgery to remove loose skin because I disliked how it looked. I have held the policy four years.
cases.why: Surgery to change appearance is excluded; it was not necessitated by an Accident, Burn or Cancer.

cases.scenario: I had my gallbladder removed. I'm 45.
cases.why: Nothing is said about how long the policy has been held, and a thirty-day initial waiting period applies to any illness in the first month, so whether the claim is payable turns on a fact not given.
